title: Gideon and the Hollow
premise: Coral Nystrom, last apprentice of the Wayfarers' Guild, has spent their life mapping the smuggler roads beneath Thornfell while hiding a forbidden gift: they can hear the dead. When the crown's witch-hunters seize Coral's mentor and sell his soul to the court beneath the mountain, Coral joins forces with Gideon Vale, a disgraced inquisitor who has turned against the hunt he once led. Together they descend through the hollow roads, trading secrets and falling into a love neither duty permits. At the mountain's heart Coral must choose between reclaiming their mentor's soul and shattering the crown's claim on all gifted souls — and they choose to break the bargain, freeing thousands at the cost of the guild's last road home.
about_author: W. M. Ishikawa is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent six years surveying mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write about borders, both drawn on maps and drawn through hearts.

chapters.title: The Last Apprentice
chapters.summary: Coral Nystrom's POV. Coral guides a smuggling run through Thornfell's fog-roads, mourning the guild that has dwindled to three members. They hide a flare of their gift — hearing a dead shepherd's voice in the stones. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened by pride in mastery of the roads.

chapters.title: A Proclamation in Ash
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. In the market town of Bellharrow, criers announce the crown's hunt for the gifted; a neighbor is dragged away. Coral burns their mother's letters to destroy evidence of the gift. Beat: fear curdling into defiance as Coral chooses to stay rather than flee.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor Who Fell
chapters.summary: Gideon Vale's POV. Gideon, once the hunt's most feared inquisitor, refuses an order to burn a gifted child and is branded a traitor. He flees into Thornfell knowing only Coral's guild can navigate it. Beat: shame transmuted into grim resolve.

chapters.title: Knifepoint Negotiations
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Coral catches Gideon trespassing on guild roads; knives are drawn, then lowered when Gideon reveals the hunt's true purpose: harvesting souls for the court beneath the mountain. Beat: wary alliance forged from mutual hatred of the crown.

chapters.title: What the Dead Told Me
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral confesses their gift to Gideon by letting him hear the dead shepherd's voice. Gideon, who built his career denying such things, is shaken. Beat: vulnerability exchanged like currency, trust tentatively begun.

chapters.title: Master Aldric Taken
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Witch-hunters raid the guildhall; Coral's mentor Aldric covers their escape and is captured alive — because the crown wants souls intact. Coral watches from hiding, unable to act. Beat: guilt and grief igniting the quest.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Souls
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon decodes his old inquisitor's ledger: Aldric's soul will be sold at the solstice court beneath Thornfell, twenty days hence. He also finds his own name listed among future harvests. Beat: cold horror becoming personal stakes.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The pair takes the Hollow Road, a passage that shifts with memory. Coral teaches Gideon the guild's craft; he teaches her how hunters think. Beat: intimacy growing through shared competence and banter.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse Ghosts
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At an abandoned tollhouse, the dead crowd Coral's senses, demanding justice for a massacre the crown buried. Gideon recognizes his old commander's seal on the orders. Beat: Coral's gift reframed from curse to instrument of justice.

chapters.title: Ambush at Greywater Span
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Hunters led by Gideon's former partner Sera Kest ambush the bridge. Gideon takes a crossbow bolt meant for Coral; they escape into the river caves. Beat: love admitted silently in the moment of near-loss.

chapters.title: Fever and Confessions
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. While Gideon fights infection, Coral keeps vigil and speaks truths aloud that they cannot say to his waking face. Gideon, half-lucid, answers in kind. Beat: the love against duty theme made explicit and tender.

chapters.title: Sera's Offer
chapters.summary: Sera Kest's POV. Sera tracks them but hesitates; she has begun hearing her harvested brother's voice. She offers Coral a deal: the court's back entrance in exchange for proof her brother's soul survives. Beat: enemy complicated into reluctant ally.

chapters.title: The Door Beneath the Falls
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Using Sera's route and Coral's maps, they find the hidden gate into the under-mountain. The dead of centuries whisper warnings from the threshold. Beat: dread and awe as the plan becomes real and irreversible.

chapters.title: Court of Borrowed Faces
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Disguised as soul-brokers, they infiltrate the court, where nobles wear stolen identities. Coral hears hundreds of imprisoned souls singing in the walls. Beat: horror at scale, resolve hardened into purpose beyond one rescue.

chapters.title: Aldric, Sold
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. They find Aldric's body alive but hollowed, his soul already entered into the auction. He begs Coral not to damn themselves for him. Beat: the mission's cost made flesh; Coral refuses to leave.

chapters.title: The Auction of Names
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The solstice auction begins. Gideon publicly renounces the crown, using his inquisitor credentials to halt proceedings and expose the ledger. Chaos erupts; Sera turns her hunters aside. Beat: justice outside the law, loudly claimed.

chapters.title: The Bargain Beneath
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The court's sovereign offers Coral a trade: Aldric's soul for Coral's own gift-bound soul, which would make the guild's roads truly unbreakable. Coral nearly accepts. Beat: temptation at its most seductive — identity offered as a cage.

chapters.title: Break the Seal
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Instead of bargaining, Coral uses their gift to rouse every imprisoned soul at once; Gideon strikes the sovereign's seal with the inquisitor's blade. The mountain convulses. Beat: climax — collective liberation over private salvation.

chapters.title: The Long Way Up
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Fleeing the collapsing court, they carry Aldric's rekindled soul-shard while the dead guide them out through roads only ghosts remember. Sera holds the gate. Beat: desperate, luminous escape powered by everything Coral once feared.

chapters.title: What the Guild Owes
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Above ground, Aldric wakes diminished but himself. The guild is three again — plus two. Coral reckons with what was lost: the old roads, the old secrecy. Beat: bittersweet accounting, grief braided with gratitude.

chapters.title: Hunters No More
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera delivers the ledger to the capital's press, ending her own career and the hunt's legitimacy. She and Gideon make an uneasy peace. Beat: justice institutionalized at personal cost; the law finally bends toward right.

chapters.title: A Road With Two Names
chapters.summary: Coral and Gideon's shared POV. The epilogue-in-scene: Coral carves a new map — no longer smugglers' roads but open ways for the gifted, with Gideon walking beside them. The dead sing softly in the stones. Beat: identity remade; love and duty reconciled into a shared calling.
